SMTO-WEB-0032 — Part of the answer says more than SMTO's research shows

GUID: 3227d9ba-5088-57f2-8d44-9050f7cbf08e
Slug: research-unsupported-claim
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • Some of the answer goes beyond what the pages SMTO read actually show. SMTO won't present that part as checked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to remove or back up the unsupported parts. The check found text, such as opinions or conclusions, that no page SMTO read supports.
  2. If the run stops, ask SMTO for just the facts it found, each with its source. A fact-only answer is easier to back up with the pages SMTO read.
  3. If the run stops and an unchecked answer is acceptable to you, open the Research proof validation card shown in the run and turn off Enforce this check for this run. This shows the full answer, including statements SMTO couldn't back up.

What success looks like

  • The answer appears and every statement in it has a source or is marked as unconfirmed.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat the unsupported parts of an answer as checked facts.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof found an unsupported assertion: a claim with no eligible selected facts or evidence spans, a derivation or reasoned-conclusion claim over non-deterministic facts, or substantive answer text left outside claim coverage.

What this means

  • A claim has no eligible selected facts or spans, asserts an unregistered semantic derivation, or leaves substantive answer text outside claim coverage. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • A claim has no eligible selected facts or spans, asserts an unregistered semantic derivation, or leaves substantive answer text outside claim coverage.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect empty fact selection, missing evidence, inference type and uncovered prose.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_unsupported_claim from selected_facts (no usable fact refs), _verify_fact (fact without evidence_ids) or _validate_answer (unregistered semantic inference, or residual uncovered text after removing claim markers). Cover every substantive sentence with a verified claim, drop unsupported assertions, or use [[research_summary]] / status partial for a scoped limitation.
  • Remove unsupported assertions, use verified facts, or report a scoped limitation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • Every definite assertion has supported structured coverage, with uncertainty stated where allowed.

What not to do

  • Do not label an unsupported assertion as mechanically verified.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
